name: IRIS-T SLM

cost.display: ~€140M per fire unit (2022); missile ~€250-565K depending on variant/buyer

key_facts.label: Spec
key_facts.value: Infrared-seeking missile (immune to RF jamming, unlike radar-guided types)

characteristics: Infrared-seeking missile (immune to RF jamming, unlike radar-guided types)
Strength: Highest reported intercept rate of any deployed system in Ukraine (~99%, 240+ confirmed kills incl. a single engagement downing 15 cruise missiles)
Limitation: Limited numbers relative to the scale of Russian strike campaigns; IR seeker can be affected by flares/decoys in theory though not widely reported as exploited yet
Estimated quantity available: Multiple systems delivered under a $1.4B German package (2023) plus follow-on deliveries
employment_notes: German IRIS-T deliveries (from Nov 2022) became one of the standout performers of the air defense campaign; its immunity to RF jamming is a direct answer to the EW-saturated environment described elsewhere in this war
contrast_vs_traditional: IRIS-T SLM repurposes an air-to-air missile design into a ground-launched medium-range interceptor — not the purpose-built system Cold War SAM doctrine would have specified, but a pragmatic stretch of existing NATO inventory to cover a gap. That kind of improvisation under saturation, not a clean doctrinal fit, is closer to how this war's air-defense picture has actually been assembled.

sources.label: Militarnyi — IRIS-T SLM tested in Ukraine
